# A template comment may hold anything, including an apostrophe and
# unbalanced quotes. Scanning has to take the comment as a unit, or the
# apostrophe reads as an unterminated character constant and every action
# after the comment is lost -- along with every mutant in it.
#
# The comment here also carries a trim marker, which comes between the left
# delimiter and the /* that opens the comment.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}{{- /*
you'd want "quotes" and `backticks` here
*/}}<p>{{.Name}}</p>{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Name string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "<p>World</p>"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
